entities.name: Anax
entities.description: Eldest son of King Athanas and prince of Akros; smaller than his brother and disliked by his father, he trains to prove himself fit to rule.

entities.name: Timoteus
entities.description: Anax's younger brother, larger and stronger, whom their father favors as heir.

entities.name: Pelagia
entities.description: Sister of Anax and Timoteus, standing with the royal family at the audience.

entities.name: King Athanas
entities.description: King of Akros and father of Anax, Timoteus and Pelagia; he scorns Anax and takes pride in Timoteus.

entities.name: Georgios
entities.description: Aging personal tutor to King Athanas's children who teaches Anax rhetoric through 'theses'.

entities.name: Zotikos
entities.description: Older, stronger boy and son of a common foot soldier who coaches Anax in the gymnasium and becomes his friend.

entities.name: Akros
entities.description: The realm ruled by King Athanas, home to the royal palace and gymnasium.

entities.name: Setessa
entities.description: Rival power whose ambassador fails to reach an accord with Akros and threatens to bring an army.

entities.name: Akroan army
entities.description: The warriors of Akros who assemble to witness the audience with the Setessans.

entities.name: Iroan Games
entities.description: Upcoming games in four months at which Anax must compete in a junior-division event.

events.summary: Anax runs around the gymnasium and the palace grounds on the morning of the Setessans' audience.
events.quote: He ran past the rack of spears and swords

events.summary: In the bathhouse, Timoteus mocks Anax, asking whether his plan is to run away when the Setessan army is bored of talking.
events.quote: When the Setessan army is bored of talking, is your plan to run away?

events.summary: The Setessan ambassador fails to reach an accord with King Athanas and hints they may take it up with his heir, Timoteus.
events.quote: We may take this up with your heir.

events.summary: Athanas declares that Anax is his eldest, and the ambassador seems unimpressed by Anax.
Athanas dismisses the ambassador as part of a council of cowards and vows to crush the Setessans if they come.
events.quote: But if they do, we will crush them.

events.summary: Athanas looks proudly at Timoteus and contemptuously at Anax in front of the soldiers.
events.quote: and he did nothing to conceal his contempt.

events.summary: Anax concludes in a lesson with Georgios that his father may not like him and that a king's choice of heir matters; Georgios hints a king could change the inheritance law.
events.quote: Does the king have the authority to change laws?

events.summary: Anax meets Zotikos in the gymnasium sand pit; Zotikos teaches him weight exercises and the apron-running drill.
events.quote: Plant your feet at shoulder width.

events.summary: Anax asks to meet Zotikos each evening, and Zotikos agrees after a calculating pause.
events.quote: Zotikos considered for a moment too long, and gave a calculating smile.

events.summary: Zotikos admits he helps Anax because he is the prince, wants to surpass his father's station, and thought Anax was looking for a friend.
events.quote: And it seemed like you were looking for a friend.

events.summary: Anax tells Zotikos to drop his titles in the gymnasium, where he is simply Anax.
Georgios reminds Anax that the Iroan Games come in four months and he must compete; Timoteus has begun training for the pankration.
events.quote: the Iroan Games will take place in four months

events.summary: Anax resolves to attack boldly at his rival's strength and tells Zotikos he has some ideas.

relations.note: Anax is the king's eldest son.
relations.quote: Anax was, however, the first son of King Athanas
Anax was the elder by two years

relations.note: Personal tutor to the king's children.
relations.quote: the aging man who served as the personal tutor to King Athanas's children
And it seemed like you were looking for a friend.

relations.note: The two realms failed to reach an accord and Akros expects a battle.
relations.quote: it is most unfortunate that we could not come to an accord.
